title: Strapline in action
slide_intent: Judge the relationship between logo and invitation across the surfaces a reader actually sees. A brochure offers a separate sign-off surface, while a poster has to carry both elements at once.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can retain a recognizable sign-off across printed, digital and small physical applications.
demonstration: A brochure mockup, web example and pair of pens share the middle field. A separate portrait poster at right places the mark and strapline on the same surface.
practical_value: Use the back cover when a brochure benefits from a closing sign-off. On a single-surface poster, keep the invitation visible with the logo.

content_islands.name: Introduction
content_islands.spec: Place the section rail and guidance on communication format in the left column.

content_islands.name: Multisurface examples
content_islands.spec: Arrange the brochure front and back together above the web and pen examples. Keep visible the dimensions that carry the wordmark-to-strapline relationship.

content_islands.name: Poster
content_islands.spec: Use the right field for the single-surface instruction and tall poster. Keep the lower-edge signature and strapline in the displayed artwork.
